layout_structure.title_text: Scale Ambiguity Issue in Dynamic Region
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a centered title at the top in a large, plain font. The main body is organized into a two-column format. The left column contains a geometric diagram illustrating the concept of scale ambiguity. This diagram shows two camera positions at times 't' and 't+1' with a curved arrow indicating camera motion. It depicts how two different 3D object motions (a green path labeled 'correct' and a red path labeled 'wrong') can project onto the same image points (xt and xt+1) in the respective image planes (It and It+1). The right column contains two bullet points that correspond to the colors in the diagram. The first bullet point, with green text, states that depth and object motion are correct, followed by a centered equation for photometric loss (Lp) equaling zero. The second bullet point, with red text, states that depth and object motion are wrong, followed by the identical equation, highlighting the ambiguity. Below these, a faded gray line of text and symbols indicates that a zero loss does not necessarily imply accurate depth. The overall design is clean with a white background and light text density.

The slide features a large, plain-text title 'Method' positioned at the top-left. The central content is a complex horizontal flowchart depicting a neural network architecture. The diagram is organized into three parallel horizontal tracks on the left. The top track shows an input image passing through a pink 'Scene depth network' box to generate a scene depth map. The middle track shows a masked object image passing through an orange 'Object depth network' box to generate an object depth map. The bottom track shows the input image passing through a yellow 'Final depth network' box. In the center-right, a grey box labeled 'Depth Scale Alignment (DSA) module' integrates the scene and object depth maps along with two binary masks shown on the far right. The output of this module, indicated by a dashed arrow, is a 'Pseudo depth label' map. A purple diamond labeled 'L_depth' sits between the final depth network's output and the pseudo depth label, representing a loss function. The background is white, and a small page number '6' is visible in the bottom-right corner. Text density is light, primarily consisting of labels within the diagram's components.

The slide features a large, plain-text title 'Pseudo Depth Label' positioned in the top-left corner. The left path shows an input street scene image (I_r) being processed by a 'Scene depth network' (pink box) to produce a full-scene depth map (D_r^scene). The right path shows a masked object image (M_r^o ⊙ I_r) being processed by an 'Object depth network' (orange box) to produce an object-specific depth map (D_r^o), which is then further processed into a scaled version (β^o D^o).
